note: Issue #401: LAN play. One player hosts from F11 > Game, friends on the same wifi join by the host's address. Read by src/systems/net/net_session.gd. port: the UDP port the host listens on. max_players counts the host. send_rate: state packets a second each player sends. name_max: letters in a player's name. spawn_by_t89_m: how far from T-89 a guest stands on arrival. smooth_rate: how fast a remote body closes on where it was last heard (1/s); snap_m: further off than this it jumps. name_height: metres above the feet of the floating name. connect_timeout: seconds a join waits for the host before giving up. friendly_fire: your bolts and blade hurt the other players (each game applies the hits on its own player, times friendly_fire_scale); off, they pass through. hitbox_radius / hitbox_height: the other players' bodies, for shots and for walking into. outfit_check_s: how often each game looks whether you changed what you wear, and tells the others. Issue #401 (guests' ships): each guest arrives next to a free landing pad (a town box of kind 'pad' with no ship on it and no remnant_ship, the host's game decides, spawn_by_pad_m past its edge) with a ship of their own on it (guest_ship) in one of the liveries (content/look/ships.json looks), by join order, labelled ship_tag over it (ship_tag_height metres up). Call flies it to them. Every player's ship (the one they fly, else their primary) shows in the others' games; one not heard of for ship_stale_s seconds goes. No free pad: by T-89, the ship on clear ground beside the pit.
